chapter: Climax Rag and tempo and meter
title: Slow tempos and the importance of the drummer
summary: Prompted by Kid Thomas's remark that they played too fast, DeVore says New Orleans bands play moderate dance tempos and that drummers who drag can ruin a band.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Well, I noticed Thomas, you know, when you played his tune?
Yeah, we played it too fast.

Yeah. That's something else too old. Gee, that's so important. God, how could I forget that? Temples. New Orleans bands never play anything very fast. Racehorse tempo. And that's the beauty of it. That's why the drumming's so important in New Orleans band because you've got, the temples are much more moderate because the bands are always played for dancing. That's the way I figured it. And like Tom says too, you can get, you don't have to worry so much about making fast runs if fingering and that type of thing. And you can think of more tasty things to do. That's what he said in essence. And ordinarily, we do play Aldris Drutt slower, but our drummer has a tendency to drag. He only has one or two temples he can play. We start out a slow tune, real slow, like a slow drag him out blues. He'll pick up the tempo until he gets it where he's used to playing it. And the same way with the moderate tunes. That's why the drumming's so damn important. God, I can't stress that enough. A guy could, I've spent more time studying drums than I have cornet, particularly lately. Because a guy, a drummer makes or breaks it. And tempo, I mean, timekeeping, man, that is the most basic fundamental of all. But so many young drummers, they can't keep time. And that's why the best bands down here sound the best because the drummer keeps a pretty accurate time.
